editorial:
Imagine a quiet little town in the mountains where nothing ever happens until three high-energy girls decide to shake things up. You get a fun ride as these girls try to save a dusty old hotel from being torn down by turning it into a flashy disco. The vibe is pure 80s chaos, especially when you see them clash with the grumpy mayor who thinks dance music is immoral. It feels like a giant party on screen, mixed with some silly fights between the local police and a wild group of rockers and oil-rich sheikhs who just happen to roll into town.

What really works here is the goofy energy and the way the girls use their charm to outsmart the adults. While the pacing is a bit uneven and some jokes feel dated, the sheer randomness of the plot keeps you smiling. If you love old-school comedies with bright colors and loud music, you should definitely check this out. Since it is an older flick, you might want to look for a restored 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection, or just rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night with friends.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up when the girls finally break the mayor's stubbornness. After a series of wild events and some funny bribes, the mayor and police chief realize the disco actually brings life and money to the town. The hotel is saved from the wrecking ball, and the town throws one massive party. Everyone, including the rockers and the sheikhs, joins in, proving that the young people were right all along about the power of music.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves 80s fashion and goofy comedies.
